messages:
Aria: Quick follow-up on the Decision Lattice RFC — thinking about fallback ownership when session-affinity + staged A/B mix. TL;DR: we should build a tiny arbitration shim in the runtime, not a heavy rerouter for every request.
Sam: +1. Curious about cache semantics though — if we fail over to a smaller/quantized variant, KV cache entries might be incompatible.
Priya: We can version cache keys by variant id, e.g. `cache_key = tenant|variant|prefix_hash`. That lets us expire per-variant without global flush.
Jin: Versioning avoids corruption but multiplies memory usage. For high-traffic tenants that could be 2-3x. Tradeoff.
Aria: Right — tradeoff between memory and correctness. Idea: prefer shared-read caches for immutable prefixes and per-variant for model-specific KV.
Sam: How do we detect when to switch from shared -> per-variant? runtime signal?
Priya: Use warmup probes + a short stabilization window. If warmup misses, fallback to stable with per-tenant flag.
Jin: Also need a soft-fail circuit so we don't oscillate on transient latency spikes. Something like: `if latency > SLO and error_rate > X for 30s -> divert`.
Aria: Agreed. We should keep the decision surface small: signals = {p50,p95,error_rate,queue_depth}. Combine with a hysteresis window.
OpsBot: Deploy: canary-2024-03-12T14:05 auto-switched -> stable-2024-02 due to p95 spike (15s) :rotating_light:
Sam: OpsBot data helps. But who owns rollbacks? The shim should only decide, ownership of rollout policy still belongs to platform.
Priya: That implies two interfaces: 1) policy expressiveness (platform) 2) fast decision API (runtime). Keep runtime API tiny: `evaluate(request_context) -> variant|fallback`.
Jin: Minimal API is good. Also add a `probe()` endpoint for warmup and async background warming tasks.
Aria: For telemetry we need traceability — each decision must include the rule that fired, the signals, and a decision_id to link to rollouts dashboard.
Sam: Agreed. Add a short contract: `decision = {decision_id, rule_id,signals,chosen_variant,reason}`. Lightweight JSON.
Priya: Ops consideration: per-tenant budgets. We should be able to pin a tenant to stable variant even if policy would route otherwise (billing/SLA).
Jin: Implementation sketch: runtime keeps a small in-memory decision cache + async fetch for policy from control plane. On mismatch, control plane pushes config.
Aria: Action items: prototype arbitration shim in eng-runtime (owner @Jin, ETA 2w), policy -> runtime proto (owner @Priya, ETA 1w), add decision telemetry fields in Console (owner @Sam, ETA 3w).
Sam: One more — chaos scenarios: what if control plane is unreachable? Shim must default to safe fallback (stable) and emit an alert.
Priya: Yes, default = stable; emit metric `decision_defaulted_to_stable` and a breadcrumb for postmortem.
Jin: I'll sketch the shim repo layout in a PR, include a tiny simulator for traffic patterns so we can test hysteresis and cache blowups.
Aria: Thanks. Keeping this small & observable is the win. Sync next week after initial prototype. :thumbsup:
